{

  "workflow_yaml": "# Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one

name: Snapshot Daily Release Automation
on:
  schedule: # schedule the job to run at 12 a.m. daily
    - cron: "0 0 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      branch:
        description: 'The branch to trigger the workflow, The default branch is "develop" when both branch and commit_id are empty'
        required: false
      commit_id:
        description: 'The commit id to trigger the workflow. Do not set branch and commit_id together'
        required: false
      rocketmq_version:
        description: 'Name of the SNAPSHOT version to be generated. The default version is "$VERSION-stable-SNAPSHOT"'
        required: false

env:
  MAVEN_OPTS: -Dhttp.keepAlive=false -Dmaven.wagon.http.pool=false -Dmaven.wagon.httpconnectionManager.ttlSeconds=120
  DOCKER_REPO: apache/rocketmq-ci

jobs:
  dist-tar:
    if: github.repository == 'apache/rocketmq'
    name: Build dist tar
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout develop
        if: github.event.inputs.branch == '' && github.event.inputs.commit_id == ''
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          ref: develop

      - name: Checkout specific commit
        if: github.event.inputs.branch == '' && github.event.inputs.commit_id != ''
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.commit_id }}

      - name: Checkout specific branch
        if: github.event.inputs.branch != '' && github.event.inputs.commit_id == ''
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.inputs.branch }}

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: "corretto"
          java-version: "8"
          cache: "maven"
      - name: Build distribution tar
        env:
          MAVEN_SETTINGS: ${{ github.workspace }}/.github/asf-deploy-settings.xml
        run: |
          mvn -Prelease-all -DskipTests -Dspotbugs.skip=true clean install -U
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        name: Upload distribution tar
        with:
          name: rocketmq
          path: distribution/target/rocketmq*/rocketmq*

  docker-build:
    if: ${{ success() }}
    name: Docker images
    needs: [ dist-tar ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      matrix:
        base-image: [ "ubuntu" ]
        java-version: [ "8" ]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          repository: apache/rocketmq-docker.git
          ref: master
          path: rocketmq-docker
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        name: Download distribution tar
        with:
          name: rocketmq
          path: rocketmq
      - name: docker-login
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USER }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build and save docker images
        id: build-images
        run: |
          cd rocketmq-docker/image-build-ci
          version=${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref_name }}-$(uuidgen)
          mkdir versionlist
          touch versionlist/"${version}-`echo ${{ matrix.base-image }} | sed -e "s/:/-/g"`"
          sh ./build-image-local.sh ${version} ${{ matrix.base-image }} ${{ matrix.java-version }} ${DOCKER_REPO}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        name: Upload distribution tar
        with:
          name: versionlist
          path: rocketmq-docker/image-build-ci/versionlist/*

  list-version:
    if: >
      github.repository == 'apache/rocketmq' && 
      always()
    name: List version
    needs: [ docker-build ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      version-json: ${{ steps.show_versions.outputs.version-json }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        name: Download versionlist
        with:
          name: versionlist
          path: versionlist
      - name: Show versions
        id: show_versions
        run: |
          a=(`ls versionlist`)
          printf '%s\n' "${a[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .
          echo version-json=`printf '%s\n' "${a[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .` >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  deploy-rocketmq:
    if: ${{ success() }}
    name: Deploy RocketMQ
    needs: [ list-version,docker-build ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      matrix:
        version: ${{ fromJSON(needs.list-version.outputs.version-json) }}
    steps:
      - uses: apache/rocketmq-test-tool@1a646589accad17070423eabf0f54925e52b0666
        name: Deploy rocketmq
        with:
          action: "deploy"
          ask-config: "${{ secrets.ASK_CONFIG_VIRGINA }}"
          test-version: "${{ matrix.version }}"
          chart-git: "https://github.com/apache/rocketmq-docker.git"
          chart-branch: "master"
          chart-path: "./rocketmq-k8s-helm"
          job-id: ${{ strategy.job-index }}
          helm-values: |
            nameserver:
              image:
                repository: ${{env.DOCKER_REPO}}
                tag: ${{ matrix.version }}
            broker:
              image:
                repository: ${{env.DOCKER_REPO}}
                tag: ${{ matrix.version }}
            proxy:
              image:
                repository: ${{env.DOCKER_REPO}}
                tag: ${{ matrix.version }}

  java-grpc-e2e-test:
    if: ${{ success() }}
    name: E2E Test
    needs: [ list-version, deploy-rocketmq ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      matrix:
        version: ${{ fromJSON(needs.list-version.outputs.version-json) }}
    steps:
      - uses: apache/rocketmq-test-tool@1a646589accad17070423eabf0f54925e52b0666
        name: e2e test
        with:
          action: "test"
          ask-config: "${{ secrets.ASK_CONFIG_VIRGINA }}"
          test-version: "${{ matrix.version }}"
          test-code-git: "https://github.com/apache/rocketmq-e2e.git"
          test-code-branch: "master"
          test-code-path: java/e2e
          test-cmd: "mvn -B test"
          job-id: ${{ strategy.job-index }}
      - name: Publish Test Report
        uses: mikepenz/action-junit-report@v3
        if: always() # always run even if the previous step fails
        with:
          report_paths: '**/test_report/TEST-*.xml'
          annotate_only: true
          include_passed: true
          detailed_summary: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        name: Upload test log
        with:
          name: testlog.txt
          path: testlog.txt

  clean:
    if: always()
    name: Clean
    needs: [ list-version, java-grpc-e2e-test ]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      matrix:
        version: ${{ fromJSON(needs.list-version.outputs.version-json) }}
    steps:
      - uses: apache/rocketmq-test-tool@1a646589accad17070423eabf0f54925e52b0666
        name: clean
        with:
          action: "clean"
          ask-config: "${{ secrets.ASK_CONFIG_VIRGINA }}"
          test-version: "${{ matrix.version }}"
          job-id: ${{ strategy.job-index }}

  snapshot:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 50
    needs: [ java-grpc-e2e-test ]
    env:
      NEXUS_DEPLOY_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.NEXUS_USER }}
      NEXUS_DEPLOY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.NEXUS_PW }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          ref: develop
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up JDK
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          java-version: 8
          distribution: "corretto"
          cache: "maven"
      - name: Update default pom version
        if: github.event.inputs.rocketmq_version == ''
        run: |
          VERSION=$(mvn -q -Dexec.executable='echo' -Dexec.args='${project.version}' --non-recursive exec:exec)
          VERSION=$(echo $VERSION | awk -F '-SNAPSHOT' '{print $1}')
          VERSION=$VERSION-stable-SNAPSHOT
          mvn versions:set -DnewVersion=$VERSION
      - name: Update User-defined pom version
        if: github.event.inputs.rocketmq_version != ''
        run: |
          mvn versions:set -DnewVersion=${{ github.event.inputs.rocketmq_version }}
      - name: Deploy to ASF Snapshots Repository
        timeout-minutes: 40
        run: mvn clean deploy -DskipTests=true --settings .github/asf-deploy-settings.xml",
  "rationale": "The snapshot job lacked a job-level timeout, which could allow runaway runs if the Maven deploy hangs. Adding a 50-minute timeout (with 10 minutes headroom over the 40-minute step timeout) bounds the job while preserving all build and test coverage. This change is supported by the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern and experimental evidence showing that custom timeouts reduce runaway consumption.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}

We are given a workflow for "Snapshot Daily Release Automation" for Apache RocketMQ. The workflow runs on a schedule (daily at midnight) and can be manually triggered. It has several jobs: dist-tar, docker-build, list-version, deploy-rocketmq, java-grpc-e2e-test, clean, and snapshot.

We are to propose an evidence-supported CI optimization that fits this workflow, preserving build and test coverage, and avoiding unrelated changes. We must use the retrieved evidence and repository files to check prerequisites.

Looking at the evidence, we have several experiment examples and patterns. The patterns include:
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure.
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: Bound jobs with a custom timeout.
- P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE: Share cached build dependencies (e.g., pip cache).
- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Cache dependency downloads (Maven cache is already used in the workflow?).

We need to see which optimizations are applicable and supported by evidence.

First, examine the workflow for potential optimizations:

1. The workflow uses Maven with cache: "cache: \"maven\"" in setup-java. That's already caching Maven dependencies. So P-LIT-GHA-CACHE might already be applied.

2. There are matrix strategies in docker-build, deploy-rocketmq, java-grpc-e2e-test, and clean. The matrix is over versions (from list-version). The matrix size is likely small (maybe 1 version per run). However, if there are multiple versions, fail-fast could be considered. But note: the matrix is over versions, and each version is a separate deployment/test. If one fails, do we want to cancel the others? The pattern P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is about canceling remaining matrix jobs after a failure. The evidence shows synthetic experiments where fail-fast was set to true and showed some savings. However, the contraindications: "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required". In this workflow, each version is a separate release candidate? The jobs are: deploy-rocketmq, java-grpc-e2e-test, clean. They are sequential per version (needs). Actually, the matrix is in each job separately, but they are chained via needs. The matrix in deploy-rocketmq, java-grpc-e2e-test, and clean are the same versions. If one version fails in deploy, the subsequent jobs for that version might not run? Actually, the needs are at job level, not matrix level. The workflow uses needs: [ list-version, docker-build ] for deploy-rocketmq, and then java-grpc-e2e-test needs [ list-version, deploy-rocketmq ], and clean needs [ list-version, java-grpc-e2e-test ]. The matrix is per job. So if deploy-rocketmq fails for one version, the java-grpc-e2e-test for that version might still run? Actually, the needs are job-level, so if deploy-rocketmq job fails (any matrix entry?), the whole job fails? In GitHub Actions, if a job has a matrix and one matrix entry fails, the job is considered failed unless you use continue-on-error. The subsequent jobs that need this job will not run (unless they use if: always() or similar). Here, java-grpc-e2e-test needs deploy-rocketmq, so if deploy-rocketmq fails, java-grpc-e2e-test won't run. That's already a form of fail-fast at job level. But within the matrix of deploy-rocketmq, if one version fails, the other versions still run? By default, fail-fast is true for matrix. The workflow does not specify fail-fast, so it defaults to true. So if one matrix entry fails, the others are cancelled. That's already the default. So P-LIT-FAIL-FAST might not be needed.

3. Custom timeout: The jobs have timeout-minutes set (30, 30, 30, 60, 60, 60). Could we reduce them based on history? The evidence P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT shows an experiment where adding a timeout of 5 minutes reduced elapsed time by 26%. However, that was for a Node.js workflow. Our workflow has Maven builds and Docker builds and Kubernetes deployments. The timeouts are already set. Could we reduce them? We don't have historical data to set a tighter bound. The pattern P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT suggests deriving timeout from successful history. But we don't have that data. The evidence for P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is from a different type of workflow. The contraindication: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit". We don't know if the current timeouts are too generous. The workflow runs daily and has been failing at startup (according to ci_history). The failures are startup_failure, which might be due to infrastructure issues. Not sure if timeout optimization is applicable.

The pattern P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE is about sharing cached build dependencies across runners (e.g., using actions/cache with a key). The workflow already uses Maven's built-in cache?
